newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine meat firms say hit by smuggled products.
newsitem.headline: Philippine meat firms say hit by smuggled products.

text.p: Philippine meat processors urged the government on Thursday to stop the flooding of imported canned meat products in the country, which they said were smuggled into the country.

"For 1996, smuggled canned meat products is expected to reach three million cases with a wholesale value of $75 million," the Philippine Association of Meat Processors Inc (PAMPI) said in a position paper submitted to President Fidel Ramos.
PAMPI urged Ramos to penalise local retailers selling smuggled canned meat products.
Local meat processors said they could not compete with smuggled meaat products due to the high tariffs they paid on frozen beef imports.
"Local processors are forced to import beef since there are no local supplies available at competitive prices," it said.
PAMPI asked the government to allow additional importation of frozen beef "to the level of the actual requirements of all legitimate meat processors."
PAMPI said the government has approved the importation of 21,000 tonnes of frozen beef at minimal tariffs in the second half of the year, which is lower than its requirement of 33,000 tonnes.
